# package fxserver

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uafx/fxserver"
```

Package fxserver adds the information model of OPC UA FX (UAFX, OPC 10000-81 version 1.00.04) to a server.Server: the types of the UAFX Data, AutomationComponent (AC) and ConnectionManager (CM) namespaces, the Devices (DI) model of OPC 10000-100 they build on, the FxRoot object (Part 81 §12.2) and the NamespaceMetadata objects of the three UAFX namespaces (§14.1).

A server becomes an AutomationComponent with the instances an application imports with ImportNodeSet. EnableConnections serves the EstablishConnections and CloseConnections Methods of its AutomationComponents (§6.2.4, §6.2.5) with PubSub. The other Methods of the model (Verify and VerifyAsset called on their own, and the Methods of the ConnectionManager) have no implementation: the server answers a call with Bad\_MethodInvalid, as for any Method without a handler.

	srv := server.New(opts...)
	ns, err := fxserver.AddModel(srv)
	...
	err = fxserver.ImportNodeSet(srv, myAutomationComponentNodeSet)
	conns, err := fxserver.EnableConnections(srv, ns, fxserver.ConnectionOptions{})

Import the model and enable the connections before the server starts.

## Functions

### func ConfigureAdmin

```go
func ConfigureAdmin() *ua.NodeID
```

ConfigureAdmin returns the NodeId of the well-known Role ConfigureAdmin (Part 3 §4.9.2), which a [server.RoleMapper](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server#RoleMapper) grants to the sessions that may configure sets without a CMAuthorizer (§6.8.2, F.3.2).

### func ImportNodeSet

```go
func ImportNodeSet(srv *server.Server, data []byte) error
```

ImportNodeSet imports the NodeSet2 document data into srv with the namespace indexes of the server: each namespace of the NamespaceUris of the document gets the index the server has for it, or a new namespace on the server (Part 6 §F.2). Use it for the instances of an AutomationComponent, which a NodeSet describes in a namespace of its own with references to the UAFX types.

## Types

### type AssetVerifier

```go
type AssetVerifier func(ctx context.Context, asset *ua.NodeID, mode uafx.AssetVerificationMode, expected []*ua.KeyValuePair, additional []*uafx.NodeIDValuePair) (uafx.AssetVerificationResult, []ua.StatusCode, []ua.StatusCode, ua.StatusCode)
```

AssetVerifier verifies an Asset as its VerifyAsset Method does (Part 81 §6.3.3): it compares the expected values with those of the Asset in the verification mode and returns the VerificationResult, the errors of the two lists (one StatusCode per element, Tables 33 and 34) and the status of the call (Good, Uncertain, Bad\_InvalidArgument or Bad\_NotSupported, Table 32). Which values make an Asset compatible is the Asset's to say.

### type ConnectionManager

```go
type ConnectionManager struct {

	// FxRoot.ConnectionManager
	// its ConnectionConfigurationSets

	// mu guards the projection: the sets, their nodes and the edits.

	// by SetKey.String
	// by the NodeId of the set Object

	// the CM-level nodes it added

	// nil is time.Now

	// records is the ConnectionManagerLog, nil without opts.Log.

	// The events of the Manager, handled in order by loop. amu is held
	// while events are applied, so that a drain of a Method handler or of
	// Flush and the one of loop apply them in the order they came.

}
```

ConnectionManager exposes an fxcm.Manager as the ConnectionManager Object of a server (Part 81 §6.7, §12.3): its sets as ConnectionConfigurationSetType Objects, EditConnectionConfigurationSets, ProcessConnectionConfigurationSets, the events of the set state machines and, optionally, ConnectionManagerConfiguration (F.3).

#### func EnableConnectionManager

```go
func EnableConnectionManager(srv *server.Server, ns Namespaces, opts ConnectionManagerOptions) (*ConnectionManager, error)
```

EnableConnectionManager exposes opts.Manager on srv, which must have the UAFX CM model (AddModel with ModelCM): the sets of the Manager below FxRoot.ConnectionManager.ConnectionConfigurationSets, the Methods EditConnectionConfigurationSets and ProcessConnectionConfigurationSets, AggregatedCurrentState, the Diagnostics counters and Capabilities (§6.7.2, §6.7.6), and with opts.File ConnectionManagerConfiguration (F.3). It adds a Guard to srv, which releases the Lock of a set in edit when its session ends (§6.7.4): call it before srv starts.

#### func (ConnectionManager) Close

```go
func (c *ConnectionManager) Close() error
```

Close stops following the Manager. The nodes and Methods stay; the Methods fail with Bad\_Shutdown.

#### func (ConnectionManager) Flush

```go
func (c *ConnectionManager) Flush()
```

Flush applies the events the Manager reported so far to the address space: a caller that changed the Manager directly sees the change in the nodes afterwards.

#### func (ConnectionManager) Log

```go
func (c *ConnectionManager) Log() *Log
```

Log returns the ConnectionManagerLog (Part 81 §6.7.2), nil without ConnectionManagerOptions.Log. The application may add its own records ("LogObject records can also be generated without the generation of an Event", §6.7.2).

#### func (ConnectionManager) SetNode

```go
func (c *ConnectionManager) SetNode(key fxcm.SetKey) (*ua.NodeID, bool)
```

SetNode returns the NodeId of the ConnectionConfigurationSet Object of key, false when the Manager has no such set.

### type Connections

```go
type Connections struct {

	// call serializes EstablishConnections and CloseConnections, which Part
	// 81 makes atomic (§6.2.4.3.9.1, §6.2.4.3.10.1, §6.2.5.2).

	// closed: Close ran; the Methods that write the store are refused.
	// Set with call held.

	// by NodeId

	// created are the PubSubConnections, groups and PublishedDataSets an
	// EstablishConnections call added (ElementAdd) for the DataSetReader or
	// DataSetWriter of an endpoint; CloseConnections with Remove removes
	// them once nothing uses them (Part 81 §6.2.5.2). Guarded by mu.

	// beforeExpire, when set by a test, runs after the monitor found an
	// expired CleanupTimeout and before it takes c.call; guarded by mu.

	// beforeUpdate, when set by a test, runs in SetCommunicationConfigurationCmd
	// right before the PubSub configuration is applied; guarded by mu.

	// afterChange, when set by a test, runs after each PubSub transaction
	// of change with its result, outside the transaction; guarded by mu.

	// retryCleanup is the shortest time after which a failed cleanup is
	// tried again; guarded by mu.

	// pers keeps the persistent endpoints; nil without a Store.

	// keys pulls the keys of the secured groups; nil without
	// ConnectionOptions.SecurityKeys.

	// crash, when set by a test, runs at the points of the persistence
	// protocols.

}
```

Connections serves the connection Methods of the AutomationComponents of a server: EstablishConnections (Part 81 §6.2.4) and CloseConnections (§6.2.5) with the PubSub communication model, the Status of the PubSubConnectionEndpoints (§6.6.3) and the CommHealth and OperationalHealth they make up (§6.4.8, §10.34, §9.1.2).

It serves the ControlGroups of the FunctionalEntities (§6.5): their Methods EstablishControl, ReleaseControl and ReassignControl, the LockingServices of their ListToBlock and ListToRestrict (OPC 10000-100 §7), EstablishControlCmd and ReassignControlCmd, and it rejects the writes and calls the Locks forbid with Bad\_Locked, with a [server.Guard](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server#Guard) that EnableConnections adds to the server when there are ControlGroups.

With a Store (ConnectionOptions.Store) it supports persistent ConnectionEndpoints (IsPersistent, SupportsPersistence, Part 81 §5.5.5, §6.6.2): it stores them and restores them when EnableConnections runs again after a restart. Without one they fail with Bad\_NotSupported.

#### func EnableConnections

```go
func EnableConnections(srv *server.Server, ns Namespaces, opts ConnectionOptions) (*Connections, error)
```

EnableConnections makes srv serve EstablishConnections and CloseConnections on every AutomationComponent below FxRoot. It needs the AC and Data models (ns, from AddModel), the instances of the AutomationComponents (ImportNodeSet) and a PubSub runtime with its information model ([server.WithPubSub](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server#WithPubSub)). It adopts the PubSubConnectionEndpoints the AutomationComponents have already: their Status follows the DataSetReader and DataSetWriter their ToDataSetReader and ToDataSetWriter References point to.

Call it before the server starts; Close stops the Status updates.

#### func (Connections) Close

```go
func (c *Connections) Close() error
```

Close stops the Status updates, the CleanupTimeout of the endpoints and the settling of the store, and removes the PubSub configuration hook. The Methods stay registered, but once Close returns EstablishConnections and CloseConnections fail with Bad\_InvalidState (Part 81 Table 9: the AutomationComponent cannot process them in its current state), and RetryRestore and Discard return an error: nothing writes the Store afterwards. A call that runs when Close starts finishes first. The application owns the Store and closes it after Close returns.

#### func (Connections) Discard

```go
func (c *Connections) Discard(ctx context.Context, id string) error
```

Discard deletes the quarantined record id and releases what it reserves, in one committed Apply. It removes nothing at runtime: a quarantined record restored nothing (design §4.7). After Close it returns an error.

```go
func (c *Connections) Endpoints() []*ua.NodeID
```

Endpoints returns the NodeIds of the ConnectionEndpoints the connections manage.

#### func (Connections) Log

```go
func (c *Connections) Log(ac *ua.NodeID) *Log
```

Log returns the AutomationComponentLog of the AutomationComponent ac (Part 81 §6.2.2), nil without ConnectionOptions.Log or for a node that is not one of its AutomationComponents. The application may add its own records ("LogObject records can also be generated without the generation of an Event", §6.2.2).

#### func (Connections) OwnsPubSubComponent

```go
func (c *Connections) OwnsPubSubComponent(ch *server.PubSubChange, kind pubsub.ComponentKind, path []string) bool
```

OwnsPubSubComponent reports whether the component of kind at path is the Connections': it is added by a change of an EstablishConnections call itself (until the call ends: PersistPubSubConfiguration then hands what no endpoint uses over to the store of the server), it is a PubSubConnection, group or PublishedDataSet a call created, or a DataSetReader or DataSetWriter an endpoint owns, or a component record says a call created it. It is called in the PubSub transaction.

#### func (Connections) Persistence

```go
func (c *Connections) Persistence() PersistenceStatus
```

Persistence returns the state of the persistent ConnectionEndpoints.

#### func (Connections) Quarantined

```go
func (c *Connections) Quarantined() []QuarantinedEndpoint
```

Quarantined returns the quarantined records (design §4.7).

#### func (Connections) RefreshHealth

```go
func (c *Connections) RefreshHealth()
```

RefreshHealth recomputes the AggregatedOperationalHealth of every AutomationComponent (Part 81 §9.1.2) from the OperationalHealth of its top-level FunctionalEntities. Call it after changing the bits of an OperationalHealth the connections do not own (16 to 31), or the FunctionalEntities: between calls of the Methods the health follows changes of the Status of the endpoints only.

#### func (Connections) RetryRestore

```go
func (c *Connections) RetryRestore(ctx context.Context, id string) error
```

RetryRestore restores the quarantined record id again: when it is restored, its record goes back where the persistent endpoints are, in one committed Apply; else it stays quarantined with the new reason. After Close it returns an error.

#### func (Connections) Status

```go
func (c *Connections) Status(endpoint *ua.NodeID) (uafx.ConnectionEndpointStatus, bool)
```

Status returns the Status of the ConnectionEndpoint endpoint, and false if the connections do not manage it.

### type ControlAuthorizer

```go
type ControlAuthorizer func(ctx context.Context, r ControlRequest) ua.StatusCode
```

ControlAuthorizer decides a ControlRequest: [ua.StatusOK](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/ua#StatusOK) allows it, any other StatusCode is the result of the Method or command, usually Bad\_UserAccessDenied (Part 81 Tables 65, 67 and 70, OPC 10000-100 §7.2). It runs before the operation, under the lock that serializes the connection Methods: it must not call them.

### type Log

```go
type Log struct {

	// identifies the continuation points of the log

	// by (time, seq)

	// gone is the greatest key a deleted record had; valid with lost.

	// time.Now; tests replace it

}
```

Log is a LogObject (OPC 10000-26 §5): the records of a log, oldest first, and its GetRecords Method. It is safe for concurrent use.

#### func (Log) Add

```go
func (l *Log) Add(r ua.LogRecord)
```

Add adds r to the log, unless its Severity is below the MinimumSeverity (§5.2). A zero Time is the time of the call; the time is kept in UTC with the 100 ns resolution of a DateTime (OPC 10000-6 §5.2.2.5), and a Severity outside 1 to 1000 is moved into that range (§5.5 Table 8). When the log is full, the oldest record is deleted (MaxRecords, §5.2). The log keeps r: the caller must not change it, or what it points to, afterwards.

#### func (Log) Node

```go
func (l *Log) Node() *ua.NodeID
```

Node returns the NodeId of the LogObject.

#### func (Log) Records

```go
func (l *Log) Records() []*ua.LogRecord
```

Records returns the records of the log, oldest first. They must not be changed.

### type LogOptions

```go
type LogOptions struct {
	// MaxRecords is the capacity of the log, its MaxRecords Property
	// (§5.2): when the log holds MaxRecords records, a new record deletes
	// the oldest one. 0: DefaultLogMaxRecords.
	MaxRecords uint32
	// MinimumSeverity is the MinimumSeverity Property (§5.2): a record with
	// a lower Severity is not kept. 0: no restriction and no Property;
	// otherwise 1 to 1000.

```

LogOptions configure a LogObject of OPC 10000-26 (§5): the AutomationComponentLog of the AutomationComponents (Part 81 §6.2.2) or the ConnectionManagerLog (§6.7.2). The records are kept in memory: a restart of the process loses them.

```go
type Namespaces struct {
	DI   uint16 // http://opcfoundation.org/UA/DI/
	Data uint16 // http://opcfoundation.org/UA/FX/Data/
	AC   uint16 // http://opcfoundation.org/UA/FX/AC/
	CM   uint16 // http://opcfoundation.org/UA/FX/CM/
}
```

Namespaces are the namespace indexes of the UAFX model on a server. An index of 0 is a namespace the server does not have.

#### func AddModel

```go
func AddModel(srv *server.Server, models ...Model) (Namespaces, error)
```

AddModel imports the UAFX model into srv: the Data namespace, which a UAFX server must have, and the AC and CM models selected by models, both when models is empty (Part 81 §14.2: a UAFX server has at least one of them).

Namespace index 1 is the namespace of the local server (Part 81 §14.2, Table 260), whose URI is the ApplicationUri of the server (Part 5 §6.3.1). A server that has no namespace besides namespace 0 gets it before the model, named by its ApplicationUri ([server.ApplicationURI](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server#ApplicationURI) or the URI of its certificate). A server without an ApplicationUri, or whose namespace 1 has another URI, is an error.

DI is imported unless the server has the DI namespace already, for example from an application that imported it before. The DI nodes the UAFX model refers to must then be on the server with the NodeClass the DI NodeSet gives them, or AddModel fails without importing anything. A UAFX namespace the server has already is an error.

#### func (Namespaces) ConnectionAdmin

```go
func (n Namespaces) ConnectionAdmin() *ua.NodeID
```

ConnectionAdmin returns the NodeId of the well-known Role ConnectionAdmin (Part 81 §5.9) in the Data namespace, which a [server.RoleMapper](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/server#RoleMapper) grants to the sessions that may establish, release and reassign control and break Locks without a ControlAuthorizer; nil without a Data namespace.

### type PersistenceStatus

```go
type PersistenceStatus struct {
	// Enabled: the connections have a store (ConnectionOptions.Store).
	Enabled bool
	// Durability is what the store survives, when it says.
	Durability fxstore.Durability
	// Store is the state of the records in the store: its revision and
	// whether a write with an unknown outcome or an owed write fences it.
	Store fxstore.DomainStatus
	// Restored are the endpoints the start restored.
	Restored []*ua.NodeID
	// Records is the number of persistent endpoints in the store.
	Records int
	// Quarantined is the number of quarantined records.
	Quarantined int
	// Diverged is the number of required writes the store refused for
	// good since the start (fxstore.ErrLimit, fxstore.ErrInvalidKey): a
	// change the runtime made that the records do not follow. The store
	// is not fenced for them.
	Diverged int
}
```

PersistenceStatus is the state of the persistent ConnectionEndpoints of a server.

### type QuarantinedEndpoint

```go
type QuarantinedEndpoint struct {
	// ID names the record for RetryRestore and Discard.
	ID string
	// AutomationComponent, Endpoint, FunctionalEntity and Name are the
	// identities of the record, nil and "" when its identity cannot be
	// read.
	AutomationComponent, Endpoint, FunctionalEntity *ua.NodeID
	Name                                            string
	// Reason is why it was not restored.
	Reason string
	// Retryable: the cause can go away (a component conflict, a
	// ControlGroup in use, a namespace not loaded yet).
	Retryable bool
	// Fences: the identities cannot be read, so the record fences the
	// EstablishConnections of its AutomationComponent (of every one when
	// its key cannot be read) and the allocation of PubSub identifiers of
	// the server.
	Fences bool
	// Component: the record is a component record that does not decode.
	Component bool
	// WriterGroupIDs and DataSetWriterIDs are the PubSub identifiers it
	// reserves.
	WriterGroupIDs, DataSetWriterIDs []uint16
	// MissingNamespaces are the namespace URIs of the record that the
	// server does not have: its NodeIds in them keep the namespace index
	// they were written with. The record is restored once they are there
	// (RetryRestore, or the next start); until then it reserves its
	// NodeIds by namespace URI.
	MissingNamespaces []string
}
```

QuarantinedEndpoint is a record of a persistent ConnectionEndpoint that the server did not restore (design §4.7, C3-D10). It is kept, and what it reserves stays reserved, until RetryRestore restores it or Discard deletes it.
